meta.title: Download ai-memory and read the changelog
meta.description: Download ai-memory {tag} for Linux, macOS and Windows, or install it with mise, the AUR or Docker. Checksums, release history and the full changelog.

hero.title: Download ai-memory {tag}
hero.lede: Released {date}. One self-contained binary per platform, each with a SHA-256 checksum next to it. MIT licensed.

builds.title: Binaries
builds.after: After unpacking, follow the setup guide: install the binary, configure the server, then launch your agent.

mac.note: Includes a launchd agent. If you download with a browser, clear the quarantine flag first.

win.note: Experimental. WSL2 with the Linux build is the supported path.

builds.upgrade: Later, a binary under a writable prefix (Linux, macOS, the Windows zip) updates itself with ai-memory upgrade: it downloads the matching release, verifies the checksum and refreshes the hooks. Packages update through their package manager.
builds.upgradeNote: Coming from 2.x? Back up the wiki and database before upgrading the server, then update clients. Migrations are forward-only; rollback needs the old binary and backup. Read the 3.0 upgrade steps.

channels.title: Package managers and containers

mise.title: mise
mise.note: Linux and macOS. Verifies the checksum for you. New releases can take about a day to appear.

aur.title: Arch Linux (AUR)
aur.note: Installs systemd units for a user or a system service.

rpm.title: Fedora (RPM)
rpm.note: x86_64 and aarch64 packages with the binary, the hook sources and the systemd units. Then follow the user or system service steps.

docker.title: Docker or Podman
docker.note: Multi-arch: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so Apple Silicon needs no emulation.

src.title: From source
src.note: Needs the Rust toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml.

channels.clients: Client machines that only send hooks to a remote server do not need the full binary. The release also ships ai-memory-install-hooks and wrapper scripts for Docker on Linux, macOS and Windows. They are listed on the release page.

changelog.title: What changed
changelog.lede: A short summary of the newest release, then the counts for the ones before it. The full changelog on GitHub has every entry.
changelog.stale: The summary for {tag} is being written. The counts below cover it, and the full changelog has every entry.

highlights.title: A dashboard for your agents
highlights.text: The web UI now groups projects, sessions, capture health and response token usage. Project tabs make activity and knowledge easier to inspect; Light, Dark and System themes are available.

highlights.title: An inbox you can use
highlights.text: See pending and sent messages without claiming them for an agent. Authorized users can address a registered harness and edit a message until it is collected.

highlights.title: Edit a page section safely
highlights.text: memory_patch_page appends or replaces a named Markdown section atomically. It checks the page identity and, for replacement, the section hash so a stale edit leaves the page unchanged.

highlights.title: Repair project identities
highlights.text: Managed launches can select a project by ID when names collide. merge-project previews a same-workspace merge by default and needs --confirm to move history and remove the source.

highlights.title: Qoder joins the supported agents
highlights.text: Qoder CLI and IDE can capture lifecycle events and use MCP through its settings file. OpenCode V1 and V2 are now detected through one OpenCode entry; older force-V2 aliases still work.

highlights.title: New retrieval evidence
highlights.text: The 3.3.0 release run scored 0.951 hit@5 with full text and 0.945 with local embeddings. A small local hit@10 drop is tracked in the report; a coding-session retrieval corpus also ships for offline checks.
